This integration connects your **SolarEdge** photovoltaic installation to
Gladys Assistant. It reads the SolarEdge Monitoring API **V2** and creates up
to four devices in Gladys: solar production, home consumption, grid exchanges
and home battery.

> **SolarEdge retired the V1 API on 3 November 2026.** Since then the old API
> keys (those of the portal, _Admin → Site Access → API Access_) are refused
> and the 1.x versions of the integration receive nothing. Version 2 uses V2:
> you create a (free) SolarEdge developer account and connect the integration
> once. See "Upgrading from version 1.x" below.
>
> This version was written from the official V2 documentation, without a real
> V2 account to test it: feedback welcome.

No extra hardware is needed: everything goes through the SolarEdge cloud, read
only. The integration never sends a command to your inverter.

## What you get

Which devices are created depends on what your installation can report: only
sites fitted with a consumption meter (a SolarEdge Modbus meter) expose
consumption and grid, and only sites with a battery expose the battery device.
The integration detects all of this on its own at startup.

### SolarEdge — Solar production

Always created.

| Reading          | Unit | Description                          |
| ---------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------ |
| Produced power   | W    | Instantaneous output of the panels   |
| Production today | kWh  | Energy produced since midnight       |
| Total production | kWh  | Lifetime counter since commissioning |

Total production is the counter of the inverter (or of the production meter),
read once a day, plus today's production.

The **revenue today** of the 1.x versions is gone: the V2 API does not provide
it.

Production this month and this year are not features: the **Solar
production** widget shows them. Gladys has no type for an energy that resets
every month or every year, and the closest one is counted by Gladys as house
consumption (see "Upgrading from version 1.1.0").

### SolarEdge — Consumption

Created when your installation has a consumption meter.

| Reading                | Unit | Description                                 |
| ---------------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Consumed power         | W    | Instantaneous consumption of the house      |
| Consumption today      | kWh  | Energy consumed since midnight              |
| Self-consumption today | kWh  | Share covered by the panels and the battery |

### SolarEdge — Grid

Created when your installation measures the grid exchanges.

| Reading        | Unit | Description                                              |
| -------------- | ---- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Grid power     | W    | **Positive** when importing, **negative** when exporting |
| Imported today | kWh  | Energy bought from the grid since midnight               |
| Exported today | kWh  | Surplus sold since midnight                              |
| Import index\* | kWh  | Energy bought from the grid since commissioning          |

\* When the SolarEdge meter measures the imported energy.

The sign of the grid power is what makes scenes interesting: "when grid power
drops below −1000 W, start the water heater" means exactly "use the surplus
instead of selling it".

The "today" energies (consumption, self-consumption, imported, exported) are
totals since midnight, published with Gladys's _index today_ type: the Gladys
energy module does not count them as consumption to bill.

### The Gladys energy module

The Gladys energy module (30-minute consumption and cost, energy dashboard,
contract) reads an **index**: a counter that only goes up. The **Import
index** is that index. It is the energy you buy from the grid, the one your
supplier bills. Gladys adds "(consumption)" and "(cost)" to it and computes
your billed consumption with your contract's rates. The house consumption is
not used as an index: it includes the self-consumed solar, which costs you
nothing.

The integration reads the import counter of the SolarEdge meter once a day and
adds today's import to it: it moves at the pace of the refreshes, and never
goes down.

If Gladys already has a Linky meter as its main meter, that meter measures the
same energy: the Import index sits under it by default, and you can turn its
history off if you do not want the duplicate.

A site without a SolarEdge meter (inverter alone) has no Import index:
SolarEdge only knows its production.

### SolarEdge — Battery

Created when your site has storage (SolarEdge Energy Bank, LG RESU…).

| Reading               | Unit | Description                                               |
| --------------------- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Charge level          | %    | Battery state of charge                                   |
| Battery power         | W    | **Positive** when charging, **negative** when discharging |
| Battery state         | text | Charging / discharging / idle / disabled                  |
| Battery low           | 0-1  | Charge level at 10 % or below                             |
| Stored energy\*       | kWh  | Energy actually available in the battery                  |
| Battery temperature\* | °C   | Internal temperature of the pack                          |

\* Only when the **Detailed battery telemetry** setting is enabled.

V2 no longer gives SolarEdge's "critical" flag (the live power flow is kept
for paid developer plans): **Battery low** now flags a charge level of 10 % or
below.

## Dashboard widgets

With Gladys 5.1 or newer, the integration offers three widgets (**Edit
dashboard** → **Add a widget**). They are built from what the integration
already holds in memory: **showing a widget never costs a SolarEdge request**,
even with ten dashboards open. Tiles and charts are bound to the device
features and update live as soon as a value is published; today's balance
comes from the last SolarEdge reading, whose time is shown as "Updated at".

The devices must have been added from the **Discovery** tab: a tile bound to a
feature Gladys does not have stays empty.

- **Energy flow** — the installation at a glance. Up to four live tiles:
  production, consumption, grid (positive when importing, negative when
  exporting) and battery (positive when charging, negative when discharging),
  depending on what your site measures. A chart of the powers (production,
  consumption and grid) over the **period** chosen in the widget settings (24
  hours or a week). Then today's balance: production, consumption,
  self-consumption, imported and exported energy, and the battery level with
  its state. The **Refresh** button reads SolarEdge right away, like the _Refresh
  now_ button of the configuration screen: it counts against the request
  budget, and once the day's budget is spent the widget says so instead of
  calling the API.
- **Solar production** — production today, this month, this year and since
  commissioning as tiles (no decimals from 1000 kWh on; month, year and total
  come from the last SolarEdge reading), the PV power curve over the chosen **period** (24
  hours, a week or a month) and the time of the last reading.
- **Battery** — the charge level gauge, the battery power, its state
  (_Charging_ in green, _Discharging_ in blue, _Idle_ or _Disabled_ in grey),
  the stored energy and the temperature when **Detailed battery telemetry** is
  enabled, and a red **Battery low** row at 10 % or below. On a site without a battery the widget simply says so.

Widgets refresh every five minutes at most, and as soon as a new SolarEdge
reading lands. The values therefore never move faster than your **refresh
interval**: the same SolarEdge credit budget applies.

## Setup

You need **Gladys 5.2 or later** (the "Connect" button came with 5.2).

### 1. Create the SolarEdge developer account and application

This is the path SolarEdge provides for homeowners ("Homeowner and
Self-Access" guide of the SolarEdge documentation). It is free.

1. Go to [https://developer.solaredge.com/](https://developer.solaredge.com/) and sign in with your
   **mySolarEdge** login (the site owner's). Fill in the developer profile: as
   company name, your own name will do (unaccented letters and digits only);
   industry "Other / Hobbyist", usage "Low - personal project". The **Free**
   plan is enabled right away: 2,000 credits a month.
2. Click **Create Application**: a name ("Gladys", for instance), the
   **Monitoring API** service, then **Site Access**.
3. In the OAuth configuration of the application:
   - **Redirect URI**: `http://localhost:8080/oauth/callback` (the address of SolarEdge's own guide for
     homeowners; nothing answers there, on purpose, see step 2);
   - **Origin URL**: leave it empty, or `http://localhost:8080` if the field
     is mandatory;
   - scopes: **SITE_DATA** and **DEVICE_DATA** (without DEVICE_DATA, only the
     production is available).
4. Copy the **Client ID** and the **Client Secret**. The secret is shown
   **only once**.
5. Note your **site ID**: mySolarEdge app, site details, or the number in the
   address bar of the [https://monitoring.solaredge.com/](https://monitoring.solaredge.com/) portal.

Only the site **owner** can connect a site. If your login is not the owner,
ask your installer to make you the owner (or use SolarEdge's site ownership
transfer form).

### 2. Connect the integration

1. Open the **Configuration** tab of the integration in Gladys.
2. Fill in the **Client ID**, the **Client Secret** and the **Site ID**, then
   **save**.
3. Press **Connect**. The SolarEdge page opens: sign in with your mySolarEdge
   login, pick the site if you have several, then approve.
4. The browser then stops on a page that does not load ("connection refused"
   or similar): that is expected. Copy the **whole** address of that page (it
   starts with `http://localhost:8080/oauth/callback?code=`), go back to
   Gladys, paste it into the **Finish the connection** action and run it. Do
   it within minutes: the code works once. The site ID is taken from that
   address, and the status turns to "connected".
5. Press **Test the connection**: the message confirms the site name and the
   list of available devices.
6. The devices show up in the **Discovery** tab, ready to be added.

Why the copy and paste: SolarEdge does not hand back the `state` parameter
Gladys needs to find its way back to your instance on its own (its sign-in page
does not forward it). The anti-forgery check is done another way: the
integration only accepts the address of a connection started from your Gladys
(the `external_id` value, which SolarEdge does send back).

The authorization renews itself every two hours. It only expires after **14
days without any refresh** (Gladys stopped for two weeks, for instance): the
connection status then says so: press **Connect** again, then **Finish the
connection**.

**Installers**: with an installer account and a **Fleet Access** application,
paste the **Fleet API key** in its field instead, without "Connect". The site
ID can stay empty when the key covers a single site; otherwise **List my
sites** gives the IDs.

### 3. The refresh rate

The free plan gives **2,000 credits a month** for the whole developer account,
and every API call costs one. Once they are spent, SolarEdge refuses
everything until the next billing cycle: the integration therefore never
spends more than 1/31 of your **Monthly credits** a day (64 on the free plan),
keeping a small reserve for your buttons.

One refresh costs:

- **2 requests** for a lone inverter (today's balance and the power);
- **1 more** with a meter (home and grid powers), unless that meter measures
  the production too;
- **1 more** with a battery, and 1 more again with **Detailed battery
  telemetry** (the temperature);
- and every day, **2 or 3 requests** for the month, the year, the total
  production and the Import index.

The integration stretches your **Refresh interval** on its own until it fits
in that budget. On the free plan, expect a reading **about every 50 minutes**
for a lone inverter, every 80 minutes with a meter, every 1 h 45 with a meter
and a battery. The **API usage** button tells the interval actually used.

With a paid plan (Business Starter: 20,000 credits), fill in your **Monthly
credits**: the interval comes down to the one you chose, 15 minutes at the
shortest (the finest resolution of the API). If other applications use the
same developer account, lower that setting accordingly.

> **Why do the devices say "every minute"?** Gladys can only wake an
> integration up at predefined rates, the slowest being one minute. That
> wake-up is a mere heartbeat: it costs no request. The integration reads
> SolarEdge on its own and publishes the values itself; a Gladys heartbeat
> only gets the last cached reading.

## Upgrading from version 1.x (V2 API)

1. Update Gladys to **5.2 or later** if needed, then the integration.
2. Follow "Setup" above: developer account, application, **Connect**. The old
   API key is no longer used (you can clear the field; left as is, it is
   ignored as soon as the application is filled in).
3. Your devices and their history are kept: same IDs, same readings. If your
   site had a tariff, the **Solar production** device shows **Update** in the
   **Discovery** tab: clicking it deletes the **Revenue today** feature, which
   V2 no longer provides (with its history). Without a click, it just stays
   frozen.
4. **Revenue today** also leaves the widgets, and the **Revenue currency**
   setting leaves the form.

## Upgrading from version 1.2.0

On a metered site, the **SolarEdge — Grid** device shows **Update** in the
**Discovery** tab: click it to add the **Import index**. Nothing is deleted.
On a site without a meter, nothing changes.

## Upgrading from version 1.1.0

Version 1.1.0 published production this month, production this year, energy
imported and exported today (and the battery's stored energy) with a type
Gladys 5.1 treats as a **consumption meter**. Gladys then added two features
of its own to each, "… (consumption)" and "… (cost)": your production and the
surplus you sell were counted as house consumption, and billed. On a site
without a meter, 1.1.0 also created a **Grid** device stuck at 0 W and a
**Revenue today** feature that never held a value.

Once the integration is updated:

1. Open the integration's **Discovery** tab. Every affected device shows
   **Update**: click it, device by device. Gladys then applies the new list of
   features:
   - the features the integration no longer publishes (production this month,
     this year, revenue today without a tariff) are **deleted, with their
     history**;
   - the "(consumption)" and "(cost)" features Gladys had added are
     **deleted, with their history**: this is what removes the false
     consumption from your energy dashboards;
   - the features that only change type (today's energies, stored energy) stay
     the same features and **keep their history**.
2. On a site **without a consumption meter**, the **SolarEdge — Grid** device
   is no longer offered at all (and the integration sends it nothing). Delete
   it from the integration's **Devices** tab: its "(consumption)" and "(cost)"
   features go with it.
3. If a widget or a scene used a deleted feature, edit it: the SolarEdge
   widgets adapt on their own.

**Until you click "Update", Gladys keeps the old types in its database** and
keeps computing a false consumption from the energy imported and exported
today, which the integration still publishes.

## Available actions

- **Test the connection** — checks the SolarEdge access, resolves the site and
  lists the devices your installation can feed.
- **List my sites** — with a Fleet key, every site it covers with its ID; with
  "Connect", the authorized site.
- **Refresh now** — reads SolarEdge right away, without waiting for the next
  cycle (within the same budget).
- **API usage** — requests used today, the daily share of the monthly credits,
  the cost of one refresh and the interval actually used.

## Troubleshooting

**"SolarEdge retired its V1 API"** — the integration has no V2 application
yet: follow "Setup".

**"SolarEdge refused access"** — check the **Site ID** (it must be the site you
authorized), and that the application has the DEVICE_DATA scope. An old V1 API
key left alone in the Fleet field ends up here too.

**"SolarEdge access expired or was refused"** — the Client Secret is wrong, or
the authorization expired (14 days without a refresh) or was revoked: check the
secret, save, then press **Connect**.

**After approving, a Gladys page says it cannot redirect you** — the SolarEdge
application still has the redirect URI
`https://my.gladysassistant.com/redirect/oauth` (advised by version 2.0.0):
that page does not work with SolarEdge and wipes the code. Replace it with
`http://localhost:8080/oauth/callback` in the SolarEdge developer console, then run **Connect** and **Finish
the connection** again.

**"Finish the connection" refuses the address** — paste the whole address,
right after approving; an address from an older connection, or from one
started before the integration restarted, is refused: press **Connect**
again.

**The Consumption and Grid devices do not appear** — your installation has no
meter (a hardware option fitted by the installer), or the application lacks
the DEVICE_DATA scope. The integration only creates a device for a value that
is actually measured.

**A reading stays empty while the others fill in** — SolarEdge does not report
it for your site. The integration never publishes 0 in place of a missing
value: a 0 could not be told from a real zero. One exception, the produced
power: a sleeping inverter (at night) sends nothing, and that is 0 W.

**The values stop moving** — the day's budget is spent (it resets at midnight
UTC), or the month's credits are (they reset at the next billing cycle). **API
usage** tells where you stand; an orange badge shows on the devices.

**An "unreachable" badge on the devices** — the SolarEdge cloud does not
answer. The integration retries on its own; its logs (`LOG_LEVEL=debug` for
the details) give the exact cause.

## Privacy

The integration only talks to `monitoringapi.solaredge.com`, read only. The
Client Secret and the Fleet key are stored by Gladys as secrets, never sent
back to the interface; the access tokens are kept by the integration in its
configuration, outside the form. During "Connect", SolarEdge sends your
browser to `localhost`, your own computer: the authorization code goes through
no other server, and it is useless without the Client Secret. No data is sent
anywhere else.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings SolarEdge asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | SolarEdge retired its V1 API (and its API keys) on 3 November 2026. To read your installation: 1. sign in at developer.solaredge.com with your mySolarEdge login and create the free developer account; 2. create an application, service Monitoring API, access "Site Access", scopes SITE_DATA and DEVICE_DATA, Redirect URI http:\/\/localhost:8080/oauth/callback; 3. paste its Client ID and Client Secret, and your site ID, then save; 4. press "Connect" and approve with your mySolarEdge login; the browser then stops on a page that does not load: copy its whole address and paste it into "Finish the connection" below. The Free plan gives 2,000 requests a month: the refresh interval adapts to it. |
| Client ID | `string` | No | Client ID of your "Site Access" application, in the SolarEdge developer console. |
| Client Secret | `secret` | No | Shown only once, when the application is created. |
| Site ID | `string` | No | Numeric id of your site (mySolarEdge app, site details; or the address bar of the monitoring portal). Required with "Connect"; can stay empty with a Fleet API key covering a single site. |
| SolarEdge access | `oauth2` | No | SolarEdge does not work with the redirect address Gladys shows under this button: declare http:\/\/localhost:8080/oauth/callback in your SolarEdge application instead. Save the fields above, connect with your mySolarEdge login (the site owner's), then finish with "Finish the connection" below. To be redone only if access expires (14 days without any refresh). |
| Fleet API key (installers) | `secret` | No | Only for an installer account with a "Fleet Access" application, instead of "Connect". Old V1 API keys no longer work. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | Wished interval between two readings. Stretched automatically to fit the monthly credits: about every 50 min for a lone inverter on the Free plan, more with a meter or a battery (see "API usage"). |
| Monthly credits | `number` | No | Monthly allowance of your SolarEdge developer account (2,000 on the Free plan, 20,000 on Business Starter). The integration spends at most 1/31 of it a day. Lower it if other applications share the account. |
| Detailed battery telemetry | `boolean` | No | Add the battery temperature. Costs one more request per refresh (so a longer interval), and only applies to sites with a battery. |

## How to install SolarEdge in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: SolarEdge appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-solaredge:2.1.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-solaredge](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-solaredge).

SolarEdge requires Gladys `>=5.2.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

SolarEdge is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
